title: Feat Tightening up Timeouts and interrupt conditions.
body:
So there is a long standing issue where the app ignores termination signals: https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3876 . This is because we have a lot of wait operations occurring on non daemon background threads.

I can see 3 possible mitigations for this:

## Make the background threads daemon threads ( I have not done this)
This has the downside of meaning that app terminations will stop tasks mid task - which could have unforseen consequences.

## Rearchitect the system to be more asyncio / task friendly. ( I have not done this - Yet)
I would probably recommend using something like https://pypi.org/project/APScheduler/. This would involve substantial breaking changes to the codebase, and I have been informed that many find these constructs harder to work with.

## Add a shutdown signal listener (This PR)
I updated our sleep operations to wait for no longer than a second, and only if the system is not shutting down. This is similar to what uvicorn does internally https://github.com/encode/uvicorn/blob/3d26ab46597b368ba45d68e8b0f65342ede8d2e6/uvicorn/server.py#L311.

I was originally hoping to use uvicorn's lifespan functionality to do this - but it waits for all connections to close before executing the shutdown event - effectively meaning it waits for our functions to finish before interrupting them. It does not provide direct access to the `should_exit` flag.

## After this PR
In the long run, instead of looking like this:
```
while True:
  if is_task_complete():
    break
  await asyncio.sleep(30)

task_finished()
```

Our code should look like this:
```
def poll_task(): 
  if is_task_complete():
    task_finished()
  else:
    scheduler.add_job(poll_task,"delay", seconds=30)
```

But this would involve introducing an additional dependency and some more drastic rearchitecture.

Query Parameter Models

Use Pydantic models for Query parameters:

from typing import Annotated, Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


app = FastAPI()


class FilterParams(BaseModel):
limit: int = Field(100, gt=0, le=100)
offset: int = Field(0, ge=0)
order_by: Literal["created_at", "updated_at"] = "created_at"
tags: list[str] = []


@​app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(filter_query: Annotated[FilterParams, Query()]):
return filter_query

from typing import Annotated

e.g.:

poetry run python -m openhands.core.cli

  File "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.12/3.12.4/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.12/lib/python3.12/asyncio/base_events.py", line 687, in run_until_complete
    return future.result()

title: Fix google cloud session manager
body: OpenHands expects the FileStore to throw a `FileNotFoundError` if a read is attempted on a missing file. The google cloud implementation was throwing a `NotFound` error instead. I added a catch and return so that they throw the same exception type. (I guess I've finally found a case where java's checked exceptions makes sense ;P)

title: feat: A user-friendly wrapper for running OpenHands in docker container.
body:
Add a user-friendly wrapper for running OpenHands in docker container - a native command line tool  implemented in Golang.
Multiple instances can be started to work in different workspaces.


---

* Launch the OpenHands Web UI in a browser

title: Remove ollama reference from documentation for now
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Remove ollama reference from documentation
---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Getting ollama to work with OpenHands is not easy. Even if you do get it to connect, it's not going to be able to do the things you want because the models are just not capable enough. For now, I've removed it from the documentation and hence support of it, until we find one or fine-tune one that works that can be added back to our docs.

title: (fix) CodeActAgent/LLM: have CTRL+C again interrupt llm retries in terminal
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

CodeActAgent and LLM completion shall react on should_exit flag (user cancellation)

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Retry process on llm completion attempt now checks the recently introduced `should_exit` flag and raises an `OperationCancelled` to end retries.
- LLM: replaced `after` with `before_sleep` retry param (only triggered on fail now)
- LLM: added `_call_completion` to encapsulate `litellm_completion` and is easier to mock in tests
- LLM: changed logging of token counts to be on a single line, like cost ist
- use newly added `OperationCancelled` exception (interim was `UserCancelledError`) to exit retry loop
- extended `test_llm.py` tests with several exception handling tests

Fixes #3965

title: [agent] LLM-based editing
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Hand-crafted editing tools have been causing a lot of problems:
-  we have issues in search/replace editing using Python (i.e., weird escapes causing newline to not work #3650)
- even if search/replace block is re-written to be parsed directly into `EditAction` which should fixed the escaping issue, the search/replace block logic might still be tricky for LLM to handle, which is evident in [this benchmark ('whole' file output performance > 'diff' output)](https://aider.chat/docs/benchmarks.html).

Cursor had an initial blog post (now removed, [original link](https://www.cursor.com/blog/instant-apply)) that talks about how "instant apply" works (#1854). In essence, the idea is 
1. Use the stronger LLM (e.g., claude 3.5) to read the original file, and propose a draft edit (e.g., omit certain locations that are not changed).
2. Use another LLM (e.g., cursor trained a specialized model, this PR uses smaller LLMs like `GPT-4o-mini` and `haiku`) to read the "original file" and "the draft edit" and re-generate the new output file (i.e., edited file).

The benefit here is that we don't need to manually implement complex logic of file editing tools to try to get the indentation right, search/replace logic clear to the agent, etc. The downside is that the "draft apply" process might introduce a bit more non-deterministic, which calls for more extensive evaluation on specifically the "file draft apply" task.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Updates 10/15/2024:

> Sharing some updates, I think we are close to having the editing PR merged! It seems the upper bound of the new editing is higher than our current main:
> 
> * **Performance-wise**: On editing PR iteration v2.4 - We got to 77/300 (25.67%) w/ sonnet by increasing the max iteration to 100 (default of our app i believe) with avg 41 turns. The main baseline got 63 / 300 (21.00%) using the same 100 iterations requiring avg 43 turns (there were some performance degradation on our main branch since `24 sep` eval - @neubig is currently helping me locating the issue now).
> * **Cost-wise**:
>   
>   * A bump to 100 max turns increases costs to about 1$ per instance (about where we were when there was no prompt caching), whereas we previously measured sonnet costs about $0.3 per issue (but there was some bug in the metric calculation so this could be under-estimate)
>   * We CAN use the default agent model as an editing model without incurring cost increases.
>     
>     * On editing PR iteration v2.4
>       
>       * Avg. agent cost per instance: 0.92 USD
>       * Avg. editor cost per instance: 0.12 USD
>       * Avg. total cost per instance: 1.04 USD
>     * On main baseline (where no LLM-based editing is used):
>       
>       * Avg. num of turns per instance: 43.02
>       * Avg. agent cost per instance: 1.27 USD
>       * Avg. editor cost per instance: 0.00 USD
>       * Avg. total cost per instance: 1.27 USD
> * Increase the file-context window from 100 to 300 lines doesn't work
>   
>   * anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 WITH 300 lines file ctx: 63/300 = 21%
>   * anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620: 77/300 = 25.7%
> * New editing PR seems to suffer less from exceeding 200k context window of Claude
>   
>   * for editing v2.4: 1/300
>   * for main branch baseline: 12/300
> 
> ALL the experiments above are performed using anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, with one run each (can't afford to run it multiple times now we increase the turns to 100 - back at square 1 where each run costs 300 bucks).
> 
> I'll gradually move pieces from the editing PR into separate PR to make it easier for code review & fixing test cases



---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

title: Runtime build fixes for OpenHands as a python library
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Make OpenHands usable as a python library, when a custom base image is used

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR addresses the following issues:
1. Problem mentioned in #3571 (OpenHands cannot be used as a python library, if a custom sandbox image is needed)
2. "poetry.lock" is distributed at `site-packages` directory, which might conflict with other libraries:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/314406a7-3e33-41c7-a062-f2484962cae4)
3. `_put_source_code_to_dir` uses `build` library to create project tarball, which is too heavy.

I published a package using my branch: https://pypi.org/project/openhands-ai-test/ and was able to run OpenHands (using library) with a custom image.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

Fix #3571

title: Fix server lock up on session init
body:
**Short description**

This fixes the issue where waiting for an agent to start / any slow agent operation locks the main runloop, so no other http requests may be served (Even in other sessions).

---

**Longer Description**

Each agent session now has an associated thread that is used to run all operations, including initialization. The thread basically contains an asyncio runtime loop.

---

To test this - Imagine you are running openhands on your local computer. Imagine also that you were to run the following script in conjunction with that:
```
import requests
from datetime import datetime
from time import sleep

if __name__ == "__main__":
    while True:
        try:
            response = requests.get("http://localhost:3000")
            print(f"{datetime.now()} response: {response.status_code}")
        except Exception as err:
            print(err)
        sleep(5)
```

While your server is running, would expect your script to print out something like this:
```
2024-09-23 12:10:47.832113 response: 200
2024-09-23 12:10:52.839559 response: 200
2024-09-23 12:10:57.848722 response: 200
2024-09-23 12:11:02.859276 response: 200
2024-09-23 12:11:07.866603 response: 200
2024-09-23 12:11:12.870330 response: 200
...
```

Instead, you get long gaps between responses when the server is starting up, or when you execute a long running operation (e.g.: prompt with `Please wait 20 seconds`) :( 
e.g.: From my server log you can see big gaps between GET requests to "/":
```
INFO:     127.0.0.1:62260 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
12:10:08 - openhands:INFO: runtime.py:191 - Waiting for sandbox to be alive...
12:10:47 - openhands:INFO: runtime.py:191 - Waiting for sandbox to be alive...
12:10:47 - openhands:INFO: runtime.py:245 - Executing action
INFO:     127.0.0.1:62272 - "GET /api/list-files HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:62298 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:62461 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:62483 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

This is because these operations happen in the main run loop and don't gracefully cede control, even when they are simply waiting - effectively they block all other server activity until complete.

My change offloads this work onto a background thread so that the main run loop does not get locked. Once this is in place, the server log looks more like this (The requests keep being serviced even though a build / selfish task is in progress):

```
12:14:49 - openhands:INFO: remote.py:55 - Build initiated with ID: e522856d-0c07-47e6-975a-0de61b506464
12:14:49 - openhands:INFO: remote.py:80 - Build status: QUEUED
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63563 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63586 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63608 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63630 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63655 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63677 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63701 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
12:15:19 - openhands:INFO: remote.py:80 - Build status: WORKING
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63727 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63751 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63773 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:63796 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```

title: fix Hyperbolic / Qwen message format
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
Fix Qwen non-vision expected message format.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This addresses a regression from https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/3832: Hyperbolic supports both vision and non-vision formats, but separately, each for the respective LLM. If the LLM doesn't have vision enabled, the API returns 400 for `role=user` messages in vision-like format. So the compromise that PR 3832 tried to make doesn't work.

This PR proposes to support the two formats for now with flags for the type of format: `vision_enabled` and `cache_enabled`. It continues to use Pydantic serialization mechanism, restructured a bit. The flag is set per Message.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4004

title: (enh) Docker runtime builder with BuildKit support, enh. caching
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Enhance Docker runtime builder with BuildKit support, improved caching, and better progress reporting.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

## Docker Runtime Builder Enhancements

This PR introduces several improvements to the Docker runtime builder, focusing on performance, logging, and error handling. 

Key changes include:

- Added back "Free Disk Space" action to nearly all workflows

- Implemented BuildKit for improved build performance and caching
  (requires `buildx` in workflows wherever images are built from within OH)
- Added support for local build cache (optional, default: False)
- Enhanced progress output and logging, incl. "rolling logs" for atty-enabled terminals (not for logging to file)
- Improved error handling and version compatibility checks
- Added a couple of new unit tests for DockerRuntimeBuilder

### Detailed Changes

#### DockerRuntimeBuilder Class
- Added version check for Docker server (must be >= 18.09)
- Method `build` now using BuildKit `buildx` via subprocess
- Added support for local build cache (optional)
- Improved progress output with real-time updates
- Enhanced error handling for various build scenarios

#### Testing
- Added new unit tests for DockerRuntimeBuilder
- Implemented live Docker image fixture for testing (using small `alpine` base image)
- Added tests for image building, existence checking, and cleanup

These changes aim to enhance the performance, reliability, and maintainability 
of the Docker runtime builder in the OpenHands project.

Make drop_params default to improve compatibility with LMs including OpenAI o1.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

The use of `drop_params` in our `llm.py` code was inconsistent, it always dropped params for async completion, and followed system defaults for synchronous completions.

This PR makes behavior consistent:
1. Always drop params by default
2. Always follow the configuration values
3. Never mess with global litellm parameters

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
Fixes https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4005
author: neubig

title: Vision and prompt caching fixes
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fix Anthropic and OpenAI vision support. Fix Hyperbolic Qwen calls. Make prompt caching default (Anthropic). Retry only transitory errors. Customize rate limits.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR proposes a few fixes:
- fix Anthropic and OpenAI vision support, when selected in the UI
- fix prompt caching to be default, users don't normally want it to not work
- retry LLM API requests only on transitory errors, not permanent errors
- fix calls to LLMs that don't support vision format (hyperbolic)
- let RateLimitError limits obey config.toml customization, they used to be customizable, but that got lost
- comments on temporary fixes; small clean ups

~add Gemini prompt caching~ Gemini really doesn't want to collaborate tonight, split out for a follow-up.
This PR was built on top of https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/4008, because prompt caching and vision build on its Message structure tweaks.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3792

title: [eval] log evaluating warnings directly to console
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Sometimes, if you run an evaluation using RemoteRuntime with too many processes, the LLM will throw rate limit warnings/errors, which only get logged to the file. It makes it hard to figure out whether that error is a rate-limit warning or a fatal LLM error (e.g., the LLM was down - it happened yesterday, and it took me quite some time to find out and recover the eval).

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- When run in multi-processing, this PR log WARNING and above directly to the console, and add a prefix of `instance_id` to help figure out which instance is having an issue.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

As mentioned in https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3767, the runtime hash you got inside `app` image and you got in development mode is different. This causes issues and requires us to manually tag "runtime" images when releasing a new version -. In contrast, ideally, these two hashs should be identical, so there's no need to specify runtime images manually when release.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR 
- fixes the issue of hash mismatch by allowing `dirhash` to ignore `.pyc` (which seems to exist in the `app` docker image) and hidden folder (there's a `openhands/.cache` inside `app` image). ---- the root cause is actually `python -m build` does not respect the `MANEFEST.in` inside `app` docker, which i tweaked a bit but didn't find a good solution there.
- Add a test in GHCR workflow to tests for this to prevent future degradation


---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3767
author: xingyaoww

title: [eval] Use `imap_unorderd` for parallizing evaluation
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Follow-up of https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/4025. This is probably the 10th attempt to fix this multiprocessing.


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Use `imap_unordered` instead of `pool.apply_async`, so results that are finished will be returned immediately, and we don't need to wait for the "first task" to finish (it happens when using `pool.apply_async`).

---

title: Fix: uvicorn reloading when python files in workspace change, & started section for debugging instructions for developers
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

* Uvicorn no longer reloads when python files in the workspace director change if you use the make file.
* Added documentation section for debugging OpenHands. The initial section includes instructions for VSCode.

---

Uvicorn `reload-exclude` must be an absolute path if it is a directory. Pattern matches will not work.

title: [agent, WIP] File edit using diff format based on Raj's #3777
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

This is a WIP experimentation/code refactor of #3777 using most utilities I've implemented in #3985.
This PR is created so i don't need to push directly to #3777 to disrupt Raj's workflow & create merge conflict monsters 🤣.


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Original from @RajWorking's PR:

> **Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG** We want to switch from our current agenskills style (similar to https://aider.chat/docs/benchmarks.html#diff-func) to Aider's diff block (https://aider.chat/docs/benchmarks.html#diff) and how that would improve the editing performance.
> 
> **Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
> 
> This PR adds a new EditAction, with logic to parse these output in diff format in the CodeActParser (translating the diff into EditAction). The EditAction is then executed inside the runtime (for now, we simply parse the diff format into search and replace blocks and manually call the existing agentskills to perform the edit)

> We use the <execute_edit> tags to enclose the diff format. For example,
> 
> ```
> <execute_edit>
> demo.py
> <<<<<<< SEARCH
>     print("hello")
> =======
>     print("goodbye")
> >>>>>>> REPLACE
> </execute_edit>
> ```

title: Fix Bash commands now do not block and actually respect the timeout
body:
* Bash commands no longer block the main runtime loop
* "Index out of range error" mitigated when getting the exit code for invalid bash scripts

---

## Bash commands no longer block the main runtime loop
Bash commands were being run in the main run loop, and have now been moved to the session thread
This means that bash commands no longer block all server operations. For example - run the heartbeat script:
```
import requests
from datetime import datetime
from time import sleep

if __name__ == "__main__":
    while True:
        try:
            response = requests.get("http://localhost:3000")
            print(f"{datetime.now()} response: {response.status_code}")
        except Exception as err:
            print(err)
        sleep(5)
```

And run the following in openhands:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6292ff28-c8e3-49b1-b52d-9bf9d7b5036c)

Prior to this change, you'll see a gap of over 10 seconds between requests made by the heartbeat script because the whole server was blocked on the `sleep 10`. In this branch, the server will not block, so requests will remain 5 seconds apart.

## "Index out of range error" mitigated when getting the exit code for invalid bash scripts

The prompt: `Write a bash script that prints "OpenHands" in ascii art` repeatedly produces broken bash scripts due to string escaping issues. Getting the exit code for these previously produced an "Index out of range" error.

title: Update state.last_error when agent failed due to LLM API failure
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

This is mainly for evaluation. Previously, an evaluation instance may silently fail because it can return `AgentFinishAction` but didn't actually set the `state.last_error`, so it is not easy to figure out whether an instance fails due to agent quality, or it is just due to LLM API issue.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR adds an additional field `error` to `AgentFinishAction` to track these error messages, and update it to `state.last_error` when detected a not empty `.error`.

title: [runtime] do not keep rebuilding from generic image
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Previously, whenever a new runtime image is built, we tag them with the newest generic tag. For example:

```
Base image = python:bookworm

# 1st time to build runtime image
FROM python:bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build>,oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm

# 2nd time: we will re-use the image `oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm` to speed up build
FROM oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build>,oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm

# 3rd time: we will re-use the image `oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm` to speed up build
FROM oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build>,oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm

...
```

`oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm` tag will be keep updated with the latest runtime image. The issue is, as we build more and more images, the layers of the latest runtime will KEEP INCREASING!

I ran into an issue of runtime image building during eval:
```
step 2/5 : RUN if [ -d /openhands/code ]; then rm -rf /openhands/code; fi
 ---> Running in 98341753bf97
max depth exceeded
```
And claude suggests: The error "max depth exceeded" typically occurs when there are too many nested layers in a Docker image. This can happen if you have many RUN commands or if you're **using a base image that already has many layers.**

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR aims to fix this issue by only tagging a runtime image with the generic tag (e.g., `oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm`) when it does not exist. This way, we always use the first generic image to speed up re-build, which should resolve this too many layer issue. 

It will look like this
```
Base image = python:bookworm

# 1st time to build runtime image
FROM python:bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build>,oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm

# 2nd time: we will re-use the image `oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm` to speed up build
FROM oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build> # <- NO GENERIC TAG NOW

# 3rd time: we will re-use the image `oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm` to speed up build
FROM oh_v0.9.4_image_python_tag_3.11-bookworm
tag=<hash_for_this_build> # <- NO GENERIC TAG NOW

...
```

title: refactor: standardize linter output data structure and interface
body: **Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG** Our previous linter implementation was mainly copy pasted from Aider, and additional hacks/extensions have made that original file have low readability :(. Also, previously, the Linter outputs unstructured error messages (in the string) that are not parsed, making it hard to display them in a uniform way to the agent. This has caused me so much pain fighting with these errors during my editing improvement PR #3985 ☹️ --- **Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions** This PR: - Proposed a unified Linter interface (`filepath` -> `list[LintResult]`), as well as the `LintResult` data structure (`line`, `column`, `file`, `message`). - Refactor all existing Python and Treesitter Linter into this standardized interface, and assemble them using the `Linter` class to dispatch different files to different linters based on file extension - Refactor all existing Python, Ruby tests into `tests/unit/linter` - Move linter to under `openhands.linter` since it is probably important enough to have it own module :) - I also added a `.visualize()` method to `LintResult` so we can easily visualize Linter error to agent now! Here's a visualized example: --- **One tricky issue: Typescript** cc @tobitege While trying to refactor Typescript, i found existing Typescript linter code requires external dependencies of `eslint` and/or `tsc`. Without those, the test cases are just dummy cases (e.g., if not installed, pass the test case). Also, those linter optionally require access to the `node_modules` folder - this means Linter can only work inside runtime & needs dependecies to work properly (which i believe we don't currently have?), further complicating the Linter setup. It seems to me that the current `TypescriptLinter` is not being used for most cases currently (e.g., dependencies are not by default installed inside the runtime image) - therefore, I suggest we temporarily remove it (already did in this PR), and fall back to use the `TreesitterBasicLinter` to lint `.ts` and `.tsx` until we have a better way to systematically bundle those dependencies in for `runtime` images. This will help us making our code base simpler & more readable for now while not losing much (most of the time, eslint were not installed?). EDIT: Here's a view of my [refactored Javascript linter code](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/compare/xw/refactor-linter...xw/refactor-linter-js?expand=1) compared against this PR --- **Link of any specific issues this addresses**

title: Fix Reducing the amount being downloaded every time the hash changes.
body: I'm**Added optional flag into the image_exists function to determine whether missing images should be pulled. (Defaults to True)** --- ## The Problem Currently as you run a local development server, your docker image may look something like this: Occasionally due to restarts and timeouts the docker build cache is cleared. It is can also be cleared manually using `docker buildx prune -f`. If you clear the build cache and then change any python file in the openhands directory, then start your server, your PC will download almost 1.7 Gb of data! This introduces quite a stall: ## The Solution [We already have a solution to this](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/b78f646b656a325ef8e2e185bbb9e67263d7750f/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L254), but it is not working: We use the generic image as a base image before trying to build the required runtime image. (In essence, we take control of caching to create a custom "save point"). This does not currently work because the `image_exists` method has [a side effect of pulling the image from the registry if it is missing](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/b78f646b656a325ef8e2e185bbb9e67263d7750f/openhands/runtime/builder/docker.py#L188). This change makes that side effect optional. I wonder if this side effect should be fully removed or the method should be renamed for clarity? I am not sure why we pull these ephemeral docker images. (Or even how pulling them actually works!)

title: fix: Allow evaluation benchmarks to pass image urls in run_controller() instead of simply passing strings
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
All the evaluation benchmarks evaluate each test sample by calling [run_controller()](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/5ccee7c8a7d8eff9f8109d8968cf4b316433bc61/openhands/core/main.py#L84) and provide task description in the function parameter as a string. However, this design will not work for tasks that have images in the task description. This PR tries to fix this issue.   

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
We change the run_controller() definition to be more generic by allowing a list of actions in the input instead of only a string. Therefore, now we can run evaluation for those tasks which involve texts and/or images as inputs by passing a list of one or more [MessageAction](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/5ccee7c8a7d8eff9f8109d8968cf4b316433bc61/openhands/events/action/message.py#L8) objects (which can store text as well as a list of image urls) to run_controller().


---

title: Add github issue resolution workflow
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
Adds the ability to resolve issues by adding the "fix-me" tag to this repo.

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR uses the newly created [OpenHands github issue resolver](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-resolver) to resolve github issues when they are tagged with `fix-me`.

A few design points are listed below:
1. The resolver is available on pypi, so it installed from there
2. The resolver requires several [repo secrets](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-resolver?tab=readme-ov-file#using-the-github-actions-workflow) to be set. I have set them for the OpenHands repo already.
3. All issues will be resolved by the [openhands-agent](https://github.com/openhands-agent) github account.
4. We had an old solve-issue workflow, which was not working, so I deprecated it for this new workflow.

If you want to see how PRs will look like, you can browse the commits [here](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/openhands-resolver/commits?author=openhands-agent).

**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
Fixes https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3232

title: (feat) Introduce Router (litellm) into LLM and LLMConfig classes
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Introduce Router and configuration (litellm) into LLM and LLMConfig classes. Resolves #4056 

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Initial PR to add configuration and use of litellm's `Router` class
- In LLM class regular completion (as before), only use router if router config incl. models exist
- Added extensive example router configuration to `config.template.toml` with multiple models
- The `load_from_toml` method loads section `router_config` as a top-tier section into apps' `llms["llm"]`
  The router's configuration is complex as it is, hanging it in toml syntax under main `llm` in the
  toml file would make this even more complex and potentially unreadable, due to nesting, imho
- Added new `test_llm_router.py` unit test file with router-related tests

**Other thoughts**
- I see this as an _add-on_, _not_ as a replacement for the existing completion logic,
  as it requires a config.toml file and a rather complex configuration.
- Its only used if such configuration exists in the config.toml file. Otherwise the regular completion mechanic is used as before.
- The router does retries internally, the specifics need to be looked up in the docs.
- From their docs: `For RateLimitError we implement exponential backoffs`

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

[litellm Routing documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing)

title: Parallelize SWE-Bench evaluation using GNU Parallel instead of multi-processing
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Python multi-processing have been causing sooo much issue for us at this point, we should looking for alternatives..

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR uses GNU parallel to parallelize evaluation via a map-reduce paradigm.
- Refactor `run_infer.py` to support (1) write instances to multiple input json files, (2) read one json file, process it, and writing to one json
- Support using GNU `parallel` to process multiple input jsons at the same time by running multiple `run_infer.py` in parallel

Version 0.31.0

Added

Improve ProxyHeadersMiddleware (#2468) and (#2231):

  • Fix the host for requests from clients running on the proxy server itself.

  • Also allow specifying IP Networks as trusted hosts. This greatly simplifies deployments on docker swarm/Kubernetes, where the reverse proxy might have a dynamic IP.

body:
This pull request fixes #4127.

This PR addresses the caching issue for the root path '/' and '/index.html' by modifying the openhands/server/listen.py file. Two new routes have been added for these paths, serving the index.html file from the ./frontend/dist directory. The Cache-Control header has been set to 'no-store, max-age=0' for both routes, effectively preventing caching. This should resolve the problem of the frontend breaking on updates due to caching. The original static file mounting remains intact for serving other static assets. These changes ensure that the frontend will update properly on each refresh, addressing the reported issue without affecting other functionality.

```toml
# API key for Modal
[core]
modal_api_token_id = "<id>"
modal_api_token_secret = "<secret>"
runtime = "modal"

runtime_container_image = "ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.9-nikolaik"

This file is identical to `openhands/runtime/client/runtime.py` except for:
- Container lifecycle control (startup/teardown)

title: Experimental: Unified external interface
body:
This is soo far in draft territory it is not even funny. It is nowhere near working or production ready. (Also, nowhere near tested). I think OpenHands founder feedback as well as community feedback is warranted. Even if  we don't fully implement it, I'd like to think it will start a conversation and at least be partly implemented.

# A Possible Refactor

## The Issue
Our API evolved over time - as a result there are things that could work more cleanly. Much of it was designed with a single user running something on their own computer. SAAS constraints were not considered as part of this, nor was threading or cancelling / interrupting tasks, or paging data. This slows down development, overcomplicates solutions, and leads to a poor user experience.

## The Broad Approach
Suppose our external API was based around `Conversations`. This Very close to our existing `Session` , but session is such an overloaded term that I think we need something more distinct (We have 2 types of session in our codebase so far - as well as the standard implementations). A conversation consists of:

* `Input tasks` - things we are asking or have asked OpenHands to do.
* `Output events` - responses from OpenHands
* `Storage` - (Workspace) the current set of files to which OpenHands has access related to the conversation.

Much like a human conversation, and OpenHands `Conversation` is roughly linear, but can have multiple participants - there can be 0 - N websockets connected to a conversation. Input tasks can occur in any order, and we need to accommodate the situation where a participant was not listening at the time when an event occurred on the server.

## The API
```
    POST   /conversation  - begin a conversation
    GET    /conversation  - list conversations (Admin Only)
    GET    /conversation-count  - count conversations (Admin Only)
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}  - get conversation info
    DELETE /conversation/{conversation_id}  - finish a conversation
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/event  - list conversation events
    POST   /conversation/{conversation_id}/event  - trigger a conversation event
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/event/{event_id}  - get a conversation event
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/task  - list conversation tasks
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/task/{task_id}  - get a conversation task
    POST   /conversation/{conversation_id}/task  - create a conversation task
    DELETE /conversation/{conversation_id}/task/{task_id}  - cancel a conversation task
    POST   /conversation/{conversation_id}/dir/{path}  - create a new directory
    POST   /conversation/{conversation_id}/file/{path}  - create a new file (touch)
    POST   /conversation/{conversation_id}/upload/{parent_path}  - upload a set of files
    DELETE /conversation/{conversation_id}/file/{path}  - delete
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/file-content/{path}
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/file/{path}
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/file-search
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/file-count
    GET    /conversation/{conversation_id}/agent-info
    WS     /conversation/{conversation_id}  - connect to an existing conversation via websocket
    WS     /conversation/  - create a new conversation and connect to it via via websocket
    WS     /firehose/  - get all events in all conversations. (Admin Only)
```
This API is really a thin veneer over the python API, and so should roughly usable in the CLI / Headless offerings.

## SAASy Features
### IDs
All id's in this system are UUIDs. Some security is based on the fact that you can't get the UUID for a conversation unless you are an admin, or the person who created it.

### Pagination
All search operations are paginated - they accept an optional page id and return a collection of results with a "next_page_id" when there are more results available. Depending on the context, they also offer other filter options.

### Better Use of OpenAPI and AsyncAPI
We use FastAPI to generate rich openapi documentation for this, and will a few tweaks we can also use AsyncAPI to document the websockets.

### Tasks are cancellable
An api is provided up front for tasks (with a fallback to asyncio’s Task.cancel()). The intent is that each task should be a good citizen and share responsibly.

### Asyncio All The Way
We fully embrace AsyncIO for tasks at least at the external level. A lot of tasks should use httpx rather than requests. Those that do not / cannot, should use `await loop.run_in_executor(coro)` to run tasks in the default thread pool executor

### Rich Reusability
This api is implementation agnostic. There is no specific mention of threads, remote runtimes, docker, kubernetes or others, but all are possible. (For example, the docker implementation is likely to be the asyncio implementation running inside a docker container).

## Progress so far...
Over the weekend I created this (really rough) implementation of this api with asyncio. I put all files in a new package - `oh`. (You'd have to run this with `poetry run uvicorn openhands.server.listen:app --reload`) I have yet to write a docker conversation implementation, implement authentication, integrate with our agents, or implement any of the constraints in our API. I really just wanted to see how long it would take and whether the result would be clean - I am actually pleased with the result so far

Here is an example of the Debug "Ticker" running (It just gives a status update for a dummy task every second)
```
const websocket = new WebSocket(`/conversation`)
websocket.onmessage = (message) => {
    const event = JSON.parse(message.data)
    const { detail } = event
    if (detail.type == "ConversationStatusUpdate" && detail.status == "READY") {
        fetch(`/conversation/${detail.conversation_id}/task`, {
            method: "POST",
            headers: {
            'Accept': 'application/json',
            'Content-Type': 'application/json'
            },
            body: JSON.stringify({
                runnable: { type: "Ticker"},
                title: "Tickety Tock!"
            })
        })
    }
}
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83c2ec92-94be-4373-ad43-8efa44983e2e)

Or even:
```
const websocket = new WebSocket(`/conversation`)
websocket.onmessage = (message) => {
    const event = JSON.parse(message.data)
    const { detail } = event
    if (detail.type == "ConversationStatusUpdate" && detail.status == "READY") {
        websocket.send(JSON.stringify({
            runnable: { type: "Ticker"},
            title: "Tickety Tock!"
        }))
    }
}
```

title: feat(runtime): use micromamba instead of mamba and fix build issue
body:
- [x] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

Improve the docker runtime build speed & fix bugs in build

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

> micromamba is a fully statically-linked, self-contained, executable. This means that the base environment is completely empty. The configuration for micromamba is slightly different, namely all environments and cache will be created by default under the MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX environment variable. There is also no pre-configured .condarc/.mambarc shipped with micromamba (they are however still read if present).

This means `micromamba` is faster to install than miniforge/mamba, which will help in evaluation scenario where you may need to build thousands of containers..

This PR:
- Switch from `miniforge3` to `micromamba`
- Use the `openhands` environment, instead of the base environment - because [No other packages should be installed to base](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/troubleshooting.html#no-other-packages-should-be-installed-to-base) and we've been using this wrong for a while - I believe this is the cause of https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4153
- Force re-build on E2E test & browser gym runtime tests

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

May fix https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4153

Should also fix https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4164


**Some explanation of how this can fix #4153 #4164**

[slack message link](https://openhands-ai.slack.com/archives/C078L0FUGUX/p1727902043562699?thread_ts=1727901562.982529&cid=C078L0FUGUX)


- You build an image from scratch with mamba x.x.8 -> oh_v0.9.7_XXX
- You skip init and rebuild a new image using `FROM oh_v0.9.7_XXX` and you try to install playwright
- while installing playwright, mamba's dependency resolver decide that you should downgrade mamba x.x.8 to x.x.7 in the base environment
- bingo -- mamba is now broken in this issue https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/4153.

The root issue is that we install useful stuff (playwright) in the base environment (where core mamba/conda reside), which is discouraged: https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/troubleshooting.html#no-other-packages-should-be-installed-to-base

title: Fix ctrl c not working during startup
body:
- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

**A SigTerm (Ctrl+C) now gracefully shuts down the server during startup**



---
Since sessions run in their own (Non Daemon) thread, they don't get a `KeyboardInterrupt` propagated to them, and so will not shut down as a result. We have mitigated this in other areas using a `should_exit` flag, but tenacity was not subject to this. I have added a `stop_if_should_exit` tenacity stop, which is used to prevent constant retries after a sigterm has been received. This is most evident when using the remote runtime while it is non functional.



---

title: Retry on litellm's APIError, which includes 502
body:
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Retry requests on APIError, which liteLLM throws for 502 (bad gateway). IMHO it makes sense to retry to on it, since it can be temporary, in the case of a proxy for example. We met this in evals with a liteLLM proxy.

Not retrying on it is due to a recent change [here](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/commit/e582806004cf4bad0934dd640ab1631841d7c664#diff-b46ec9dd4b319d75809520e34b2559fd2ce46ca4895709eae9312aa04a8fa9a4L91), when I removed the base class of APIError (OpenAIError) from retryable exceptions. OpenAIError captures a lot of permanent errors, and even APIError in litellm is like a catch-all for other stuff, but it includes 502. Including a catch-all of sorts in our retries is not a great idea either (we may retry too much, at the expense of rate limits at least), but I'll dig into this some more.

---

title: Fix: Add timeout on websocket accept
body:
- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

** Prevent background task sleeping forever if client does not finish the websocket accept protocol **



---
Consider the following python script:
```
import websockets

async def main():
  await websockets.connect("ws://localhost:3000/ws")

asyncio.run(main())
```

On our server, this will initiate a call to `websocket.accept()`, but because the protocol does not finish, the task just hangs around forever in asnycio. This is not a big deal in every day use, but:

* It could be used to clog the server with malicious requests
* If you are running a dev server and you change a file, your server will get stuck at `Waiting for background tasks to complete. (CTRL+C to force quit)`

These changes not only provide the requested documentation but also make it easily accessible to users through the settings modal in the frontend interface.

title: (arch) pluggable runtimes
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Make runtimes pluggable dynamically without changing code.
- Added unit test `test_dyn_runtime.py`

---

### Dynamic Runtime Registration

This pull request introduces a dynamic runtime registration mechanism, allowing users to add new runtimes without modifying the core `openhands` codebase.  This enhances extensibility and makes it easier to integrate custom runtimes.

**Key Changes:**

* **Default, core runtimes:** The `_registered_runtimes` dictionary serves as the single source of truth for runtime information. It is initialized directly with the core runtime definitions.
* **Added `register_runtime` Function:**  A `register_runtime` function has been added to allow dynamic registration of new runtimes.  Users can now register a runtime by providing its name, module, and class name.
* **Modified `get_runtime_cls`:** The `get_runtime_cls` function now checks `_registered_runtimes`.  If the requested runtime is not found there, it raises a `ValueError`.
* **Added Unit Tests:**  Unit tests have been added to verify the functionality of the dynamic registration and retrieval mechanism, including tests for error handling and mocking the import process.

**Benefits:**

* **Extensibility:**  Makes it easier to add and integrate new runtimes without modifying core code.
* **Maintainability:** Simplifies the runtime registration logic and reduces code duplication.
* **Testability:**  Improves testability by allowing mocking of the import process.

This change provides a more flexible and maintainable way to manage runtimes in `openhands`.
author: tobitege

title: Feat more efficient docker image naming
body:
**Faster startup and change detection in developer mode**

- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
In development mode, when we have not specified a particular docker image to use, we generate a hash to distinguish builds from each other. (So as your files change, your hash changes, and new sandbox images are generated) In oder to do this we:

1. Create a temp directory
2. [Build a tarball of the openhands package](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L32) in this directory
3. [Unpack the tarball into the temp directory](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L65)
4. [Delete the tarball](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L67)
5. [rename the directory from the tarball to "code"](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L69)
6. [Add a dockerfile](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L127) to this directory
7. [Get the md5 of this directory](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/909e332207ae25e2db23b12f65d21c8f5cf7a745/openhands/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L144)


This PR skips steps 1 - 6 shaving valuable seconds off the process. Instead, we simply get the hash of "agenthub", "openhands", and pyproject.toml.

title: Refactor embeddings
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [ ] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR proposes a refactoring of embeddings to:
- start to separate the lower level backend (embeddings, torch) from long term memory class
- add batch processing of events
- clean up the code from outdated retries (which don't work well with background threads)
- separate functions for easier profiling.

I did some profiling on cpu and metal for local embeddings, and updated the default num_workers to 3. All of this is currently not in use, disabled by config, until we get it better.

This PR is a small step towards offering some backend for experiments here, it will hopefully become less difficult to test stuff than it is when one needs to rewrite too much at once.

---

author: enyst

title: Lockup Resiliency and Asyncio Improvements
body:
- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes.

* **The '/list-files' end-point no longer locks up the server**
* **The executing actions no longer locks up the server while executing**
* **Sessions now use a common background threadpool rather than and explicit thread**
* **Remote sessions no longer register as ready before they are actually ready in the frontend**

---
Since a lot of our operations were not built with asyncio in mind, this runs many things explicitly in thread pool executors. In the long term, I think we should use asyncio and only include thread pools in a few places, but this is resilient to non-coroutines taking longer than expected and greedily hogging server resources.

I have tested this and although the list-files operation can take a long time to execute, the server is not locked while it is executing:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d23ad4cc-a0ec-42a0-b66b-acd6e6cb5236)

Testing this has included the following scenarios:

* Starting 2 sessions in the same browser at a time can lock up the server (Non Incognito)
* Issue where calling list-files before the runtime is ready locks up the server
* Issue where calling a bash command can lock up the server (e.g.: `sleep 10`)
* Issue where a prompt can lock up the server (`Sleep for 10 seconds`)

title: Fix browsing actions to be more robust
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [x] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below
Fix browsing agent parsing responses.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR proposes an adjustment to browsing actions parsing.
Browsing agent responses can be a simple command or set of commands, with no "thoughts", or can contain both, with the thought first. In the first case, no actions were parsed, so its "previous actions" was empty in the prompt. This was tested first with delegation, and it just didn't work at all with several LLMs. Tested after with UI and browsing agent.

Tested with claude, got-4o, gemini. The prompt shows in the Previous Action section a list of previous actions, e.g.

Previously: 
(after several steps of the browsing agent, Previous Actions is empty, current page never got updated either)
```
IMPORTANT! Last action is incorrect:

Think again with the current observation of the page.


# Current Page URL:
about:blank

# Current Accessibility Tree:
RootWebArea '', focused

# Previous Actions




Here is an example ...

```

After:
```
# Current Page URL:
https://www.whitehouse.gov/

# Current Accessibility Tree:
RootWebArea 'The White House', focused
	[64] banner ''
...

# Previous Actions
goto('https://www.whitehouse.gov/'))
click('69'))

Here is an example ...
```

body:
Bumps [@reduxjs/toolkit](https://github.com/reduxjs/redux-toolkit) from 2.2.7 to 2.2.8.
Release notes

Sourced from @​reduxjs/toolkit's releases.

v2.2.8

This bugfix release fixes a long-standing issue with RTK Query lazy query triggers returning stale data in some cases, fixes an error handling issue in RTK Query, and exports additional TS types.

Changelog

Lazy Query Trigger Handling

We'd had a couple long-standing issues reporting that const result = await someLazyQueryTrigger() sometimes returned stale data, especially if a mutation had just invalidated that query's tag.

We finally got a good repro of this issue and identified it as a mis-written call inside of the middleware that skipped past the necessary handling to activate the correct query status tracking in that scenario. This should now be fixed.

Other Changes

Timeout handling in RTKQ endpoints should now correctly throw a timeout-related error instead of an AbortError.

Base queries now have access to the current queryCacheKey value so it can be used in deciding query logic.

We've exported several more TS types related to query options, as some users have been depending on those even though they previously weren't part of the public API.

What's Changed

  • Export QueryExtraOptions and MutationExtraOptions by @​aryaemami59 in reduxjs/redux-toolkit#4556

  • type: export QueryReturnValue by @​hornta in reduxjs/redux-toolkit#4640

title: [Runtime] Audit HTTP Retry timeouts
body:
**More deliberate timeouts on retry operations**

- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
Ever have something not quite work and the server sits there for 5 minutes before the logs even tell you what's wrong? There was a lot of that in my last 24 hours. This has to stop! ;)

 * **Renamed the method `send_request` to `send_request_with_retry`** : This more accurately describes what it does.
 * **Removed the default timeout on `send_request_with_retry`** : Each operation is different, and there is no one size fits all for these timeouts. Now developers must think about each of these operations deliberately and supply a timeout if they want to use this function
 * **Reduced the limit on the exponential backoff** : Time between retries now starts at 4 seconds and maxes out at 20 seconds (Instead of 60 seconds). When something is ready, why wait much longer?
* **Audited each use of `send_request_with_retry`** and supplied a timeout that seems reasonable.

## Testing

Obviously, the linter gave no issues and tests passed. When deciding on timeouts, I was relatively conservative and did not change cases which may result in disruptions to Actions or builds. My efforts focused on the other lifecycle and shutdown events, where I typically reduced the retry timeout from 5 minutes to 30 seconds. I think with further testing we could eliminate a lot of these retries altogether, but I was trying to be conservative with this change.

title: Install docker in the OpenHands app image
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [ ] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

Install docker in the OpenHands app image

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Installing docker in the OpenHands app image allows it to build a sandbox image off of a SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE using the docker method. So users are able to provide a base image to the docker command without the development flow.

I tested this by:
* Building the OpenHands app image and tagging it with `myapp:1.0.0`
* Running the docker command as follows:
```
docker run -it \                                         
    -e SANDBOX_BASE_CONTAINER_IMAGE=ruby:3.3.4 \
    -e SANDBOX_USER_ID=$(id -u) \
    -e WORKSPACE_MOUNT_PATH=$WORKSPACE_BASE \
    -v $WORKSPACE_BASE:/opt/workspace_base \
    -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
    -p 3000:3000 \
    --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
    --name openhands-app-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S) \
    myapp:1.0.0 
```
* Checking that ruby 3.3.4 is installed

**I am unsure if this is the route we want to go. It seems to add 0.5GB to the app image. However, this is what I came up with after some guidance. See the issues for why this change is needed below. If this is fine, I can this method to the https://docs.all-hands.dev/modules/usage/how-to/custom-sandbox-guide doc**


---

no changelog needed

We currently get inundated with dependabot PRs. Often it's pulling in a single patch at a time.

~~By slowing down dbot, we end up making bigger version jumps less frequently, with fewer overall PRs.~~

~~There's a tradeoff here--we'll spend longer with missing patch updates. I _think_ dbot is smart enough to send us security fixes first though.~~

title: Fix Graceful cleanup of session manager
body:
**Graceful cleanup of session manager**

- [ ] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
Before this change, the session manager would try to start when the constructor was called - and this was being done when `listen.py` was loaded - so this is outside the lifecycle of FastAPI.

After this change...
* The SessionManager has explicit `__aenter__` and `__aexit__` methods so it can be used in `async with`
* The SessionManager no longer starts outside the main FastAPI event loop. - it is bound to the lifecycle of FastAPI (Starting, stopping, and Restarting with it)

title: Feat: Divided docker layer to make it easier to cache
body:
**Divided and Reordered and Docker layer for better caching. **

- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
We do a lot in that single layer at the end of the Docker Install. This PR moves some of the installs around so that they occur before we copy the code. This effectively means that the install of playwright and chromium and the `apt-get` can be cached by docker when in development mode, meaning that updates due to changing code are a lot faster.

Unfortunately, in order to do this, I had to change the spec for naming our runtime docker images - I updated the documentation with these changes.

title: feat(frontend): Improve file based routing
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**
- introduces some refactors to the app to improve the file-based routing.
- Removes outdated test files
- Refresh package-lock

- [ ] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
Refactors to the routes have also been introduced. Previously, all routes where children of the `root.tsx` route which contained the default layout (e.g., side navbar). This meant that separate screens (e.g,, a TOS) would also be children of that route and contain the same layout.

To fix this, the `root.tsx` route is the "root layout" which is just its children, and OpenHands-related routes (e.g., home screen, /app, etc...) are prefixed with `_oh` (e.g, `_oh._index` now contains the previous layout `root` did, `_oh.app` now contains the content `app` did, and so on).

You can read more about how the route file naming works [here](https://remix.run/docs/en/main/file-conventions/routes). No changes have been made to the how the user perceives the URL.

title: AgentDelegateAction: make delegate start with the task in execute tags, not the rest of the parent LLM response
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [x] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below
Fix AgentDelegateAction to send only the task to the delegate agent, not the main agent thoughts

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

It's a bit strange [to see](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/actions/runs/11263110927/job/31320302649#step:8:327) the browsing agent starting with:

```
21:12:46 - ACTION
AgentDelegateAction(agent='BrowsingAgent', inputs={'task': "Thank you for providing the current content of the file. Now, let's summarize the information from the blog article and add it to the file. I'll start by browsing the article to gather the necessary information.. I should start with: Summarize the quality and cost information of various language models from https://www.all-hands.dev/blog/evaluation-of-llms-as-coding-agents-on-swe-bench-at-30x-speed"}, thought='', action='delegate')
```

Notes on the current AgentDelegateAction object:
- AgentDelegateAction has a `thought` attribute, but the `thought` ended up empty
- the LLM (of the parent) sent a thought in its response. It got lost from `thought` property, and it was included instead into the `inputs['task']`.
- the parent LLM sent in tags <execute_browse>_Summarize the quality and cost information of various language models ..._</execute_browse>. I think the LLM responds with this _task_ for the delegate agent.

It seems to me that we need to put the contents of the `thought` in the `thought` and perhaps more importantly, keep the `task` without that part, because it can confuse the delegate LLM when it contains unintended stuff.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

title: Allow attaching to existing sessions without reinitializing the runtime
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [ ] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below
no changelog needed

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

We're working on a highly-available deployment of OpenHands, which means running multiple replicas of the app. Any given API request could connect to _any_ of these replicas, so we have to be careful about managing things in-memory.

Currently, we create a Session when a websocket connects, and stash that session in a dict in the SessionManager--i.e. we keep a reference in memory. When the user calls e.g. `/list-files`, we look up the session and connect to its runtime to list the files.

This doesn't work in an HA, multi-replica world. You might hit an instance that doesn't have your active session, leading to a 404.

In this change, all the REST endpoints create a new Conversation object, which is basically an in-progress Session. And the Conversation looks up an existing Runtime to connect to, rather than initializing a new one.

Pretty sure we need to be smarter about some async/threading when initting the runtime, but this appears to be working well for both local and remote runtimes.

One breaking-ish change: I've had to remove logic related to planning/tasks because that requires accessing an AgentController via REST. TBD on how we do this going forward.

We should really do a heavy refactor here, along the lines of what @tofarr has suggested. But this seems like a reasonable stop gap

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

Updates `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` from 4.6.2 to 5.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from eslint-plugin-react-hooks's releases.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@5.0.0 (Oct 11, 2024)

This release only contains eslint-plugin-react-hooks. Notably, new violations and support for ESLint v9 were added.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks

  • New Violations: Component names now need to start with an uppercase letter instead of a non-lowercase letter. This means _Button or _component are no longer valid. (@​kassens) in #25162
  • Add support for ESLint v9. (@​eps1lon in #28773)
  • Consider dispatch from useActionState stable. (@​eps1lon in #29665)
  • Accept as expression in callback. (@​StyleShit in #28202)
  • Accept as expressions in deps array. (@​StyleShit in #28189)
  • Treat React.use() the same as use(). (@​kassens in #27769)
  • Move use() lint to non-experimental. (@​kassens in #27768)
  • Support Flow as expressions. (@​cpojer in #27590)
  • Allow useEffect(fn, undefined). (@​kassens in #27525)
  • Disallow hooks in async functions. (@​acdlite in #27045)
  • Rename experimental useEvent to useEffectEvent. (@​sebmarkbage in #25881)
  • Lint for presence of useEvent functions in dependency lists. (@​poteto in #25512)
  • Check useEvent references instead. (@​poteto in #25319)
  • Update RulesOfHooks with useEvent rules. (@​poteto in #25285)

title: Feat: Async Goodies for OpenHands
body:
**Sandardized Asynchronous Utilities for OpenHands **

- [X] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below

---
This PR introduces an `async_utils module` Specifically, this handles currently 3 use cases:

* `async_to_sync` : I am in an async context and I want to run a standard python function in a background thread and await the result. (This will mean that the function will not block the main runloop)
* `sync_to_async` : I want to start a new asyncio runloop in a new thread and await the result. (Use `syncio.create_task` if you are in an async context and don't want to wait for the result)
* `wait_all` - I have a collection of coroutines I want to run in parallel and await the result of all of them being finished.

I also added extensive associated tests. (Given that these are low level functions, we should make sure they are robust ;) ). 
I also used these functions in some places where it was appropriate.

title: (Browsing agent) Fix send_msg_to_user
body:
**End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

- [x] Include this change in the Release Notes. If checked, you must provide an **end-user friendly** description for your change below
Fix syntax error in the browsing agent

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

One more issue with the browsing agent's parsing robustness. This PR attempts to fix a syntax error I noticed tonight in `send_msg_to_user`. The cause comes [from here](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/2692c0c8fd98bd8ff1bb88441e749dfbd53437e1/openhands/agenthub/browsing_agent/response_parser.py#L28), when the LLM response already has a `)` but not backticks, it will get 2 `))` plus backticks, then it fails [here](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/blob/2692c0c8fd98bd8ff1bb88441e749dfbd53437e1/openhands/agenthub/browsing_agent/response_parser.py#L99) and the `ast.parse` has no mercy. (this made a swe-bench instance fail)

The original behavior (the double `))`) even works with actual browser actions e.g. `click(90))` or `click(90)` are accepted, but `send_msg_to_user` fails.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

title: fix: Resolves HumanEval Inference by replacing task_id with instance_id
body:
## **End-user friendly description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces**

This PR resolves an issue in the HumanEval benchmark's `run_infer.py` script where the code incorrectly references a column `task_id` that no longer exists. The correct column is `instance_id`. This fix ensures that the script runs without errors, making it compatible with the latest schema changes.

- [x] Include this change in the Release Notes.
End-user friendly description for the Release Notes:
"Fixes a column reference issue in run_infer.py where task_id was incorrectly used instead of instance_id."


---
## **Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
This PR refactors the Humaneval benchmark's `run_infer.py` script by replacing all occurrences of `task_id` with `instance_id` to align with the updated column naming convention. No major design changes were made, but the code now references the correct column to avoid attribute errors and ensure smooth execution of the Humaneval benchmark.


---
## **Link of any specific issues this addresses**
This PR addresses issue #4363, where an `AttributeError` occurs because the column name change from `task_id` to `instance_id` was not consistently applied throughout the file, leading to the error.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump mypy from 1.11.2 to 1.12.0
body:
Bumps [mypy](https://github.com/python/mypy) from 1.11.2 to 1.12.0.
Changelog

Sourced from mypy's changelog.

Mypy Release Notes

Next release

Mypy 1.12

We’ve just uploaded mypy 1.12 to the Python Package Index (PyPI). Mypy is a static type checker for Python. This release includes new features, performance improvements and bug fixes. You can install it as follows:

python3 -m pip install -U mypy

You can read the full documentation for this release on Read the Docs.

Support Python 3.12 Syntax for Generics (PEP 695)

Support for the new type parameter syntax introduced in Python 3.12 is now enabled by default, documented, and no longer experimental. It was available through a feature flag in mypy 1.11 as an experimental feature.

This example demonstrates the new syntax:

# Generic function
def f[T](https://github.com/python/mypy/blob/master/x: T) -> T: ...

reveal_type(f(1))  # Revealed type is 'int'


Generic class


class C[T]:
def init(self, x: T) -> None:
self.x = x


c = C('a')
reveal_type(c.x)  # Revealed type is 'str'


Type alias


type A[T] = C[list[T]]

For more information, refer to the documentation.

These improvements are included:

  • Document Python 3.12 type parameter syntax (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17816)
  • Further documentation updates (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17826)
  • Allow Self return types with contravariance (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17786)
  • Enable new type parameter syntax by default (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17798)
  • Generate error if new-style type alias used as base class (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17789)
  • Inherit variance if base class has explicit variance (Jukka Lehtosalo, PR 17787)

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@5.0.0 (Oct 11, 2024)

This release only contains eslint-plugin-react-hooks. Notably, new violations and support for ESLint v9 were added.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks

  • New Violations: Component names now need to start with an uppercase letter instead of a non-lowercase letter. This means _Button or _component are no longer valid. (@​kassens) in #25162 For example, in 
    function _Component() {
  useState()
  ^^^^^^^^ A React Hook "useState" is called in function "_Component" which is neither a Component nor a custom React Hook function.
}
    _Component should be renamed to Component.
  • Add support for ESLint v9. (@​eps1lon in #28773)
  • Consider dispatch from useActionState stable. (@​eps1lon in #29665)
  • Accept as expression in callback. (@​StyleShit in #28202)
  • Accept as expressions in deps array. (@​StyleShit in #28189)
  • Treat React.use() the same as use(). (@​kassens in #27769)
  • Move use() lint to non-experimental. (@​kassens in #27768)
  • Support Flow as expressions. (@​cpojer in #27590)
  • Allow useEffect(fn, undefined). (@​kassens in #27525)
  • Disallow hooks in async functions. (@​acdlite in #27045)
  • Rename experimental useEvent to useEffectEvent. (@​sebmarkbage in #25881)
  • Lint for presence of useEvent functions in dependency lists. (@​poteto in #25512)
  • Check useEvent references instead. (@​poteto in #25319)
  • Update RulesOfHooks with useEvent rules. (@​poteto in #25285)
